qt: to the Commission Ioan-Rareş Bogdan (PPE) Subject:

I welcome the European Commission’s commitment to ensuring respect for the rule of law and common rules, but the aggressive pace of punitive action announced in the new programme ignores the structural realities on the ground. The approach currently being taken is deeply unfair: boasts about a 10-year record high in infringement procedures (874 procedures launched) and mass referrals to the Court of Justice requesting financial sanctions, turning fines into a savage disciplinary tool; disproportionate penalisation of Eastern States for delays in the environment, waste and energy sectors, where legacy infrastructure gaps are huge and impossible to close without reasonable transitions; suffocating financial pressure from daily penalties paid from national budgets, which take away resources that could be invested in modernisation. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Why does it prioritise aggressive financial sanctions against Eastern States instead of providing tailored technical assistance and realistic compliance timelines for deficient infrastructure?
How does it assess the paradox whereby daily penalties imposed on less developed countries further weaken their fiscal capacity to co-finance European environmental projects?
Does it intend to link infringement deadlines to actual financial allocations for modernisation, recognising the major historical divides between East and West?
